behavior.description: Replace the outgoing scene with the incoming scene at one explicit timeline boundary. There is no interpolated frame or blank interval.
behavior.targetSemantics: incoming and outgoing are complete scene roles supplied by the consumer, not data-animate hooks or component selectors. Apply state to temporary scene presentation wrappers; preserve component animation state inside each scene.
behavior.boundary: For time strictly before the transition boundary use from; at the boundary and afterward use to. Set both role states atomically. Zero duration requires a state switch, not division by duration or a zero-length progress calculation.
behavior.restoration: No transform or mask is left on either scene. Incoming remains fully presented; outgoing remains hidden until its next scheduled scene lifecycle. Seeking before the boundary restores from without completion callbacks.

adaptation.coordinates: x/y are additive design-pixel offsets, rotation is additive degrees, scale is an authored-scale multiplier and opacity is absolute. The identity transforms refer to the transition wrapper, not a reset of authored component poses.
adaptation.sceneLifecycle: Keep both scenes available for deterministic seek. Let the consuming timeline own activation; this definition does not change layout display, remove scenes, or create component compatibleMotions entries.
adaptation.implementation: Implement this explicit boundary state in any runtime. Do not use asynchronous completion callbacks or a separate fade.
